name: Police Departments (Washington State)
tagline: Back-office agentic AI for WA/Seattle-area law enforcement — scoped to what's allowed, nothing that touches surveillance.
overview: Washington police departments carry heavy administrative load: public records requests, report backlogs, scheduling, and grant compliance. This blueprint is intentionally limited to back-office and administrative agentic AI — records processing, drafting assistance, scheduling, and compliance tracking. It excludes facial recognition, predictive policing, mass surveillance, and any agent that identifies or scores individuals, because those uses are restricted or require separate approval under Washington's facial recognition law (RCW 43.386) and, for Seattle agencies, the Seattle Surveillance Ordinance (SMC 14.18). No agent here touches evidence analysis, biometric matching, or case decision-making.
painPoints: Public Records Act (RCW 42.56) requests pile up faster than records staff can review and redact them
Officers lose hours per shift on incident report drafting and administrative paperwork
Shift scheduling, overtime approval, and grant/compliance reporting are manual and spreadsheet-driven
strategicImpact: Faster, more consistent Public Records Act response times without changing exemption decisions
Meaningful reduction in officer time spent on report drafting and paperwork per shift
Fewer missed grant/compliance deadlines and scheduling conflicts

singleAgents.name: Public Records Intake Agent
singleAgents.role: Classifies and routes incoming RCW 42.56 public records requests, flagging likely exemptions for human review
singleAgents.trigger: New public records request received via portal, email, or mail scan
singleAgents.output: Triaged request with suggested exemption flags and routing to a records specialist
singleAgents.roi: Faster first response and fewer missed statutory deadlines on records requests

singleAgents.name: Incident Report Drafting Assistant
singleAgents.role: Turns an officer's dictated or typed notes into a structured draft incident report
singleAgents.trigger: Officer requests a report draft after a call or at end of shift
singleAgents.output: Draft report in department format, awaiting officer review and sign-off
singleAgents.roi: Meaningful reduction in per-shift report writing time; no change to what the officer reports

singleAgents.name: Shift & Overtime Scheduling Agent
singleAgents.role: Proposes shift schedules and overtime assignments within labor rules and minimum-staffing requirements
singleAgents.trigger: Weekly scheduling cycle or unfilled shift alert
singleAgents.output: Draft schedule and overtime offer list for a supervisor to approve
singleAgents.roi: Fewer unfilled shifts and scheduling errors; supervisor keeps final approval

singleAgents.name: Grant & Compliance Reporting Agent
singleAgents.role: Tracks state/federal grant reporting deadlines and assembles required compliance documentation
singleAgents.trigger: Grant reporting period opens or deadline approaches
singleAgents.output: Pre-filled compliance report packet for staff review and submission
singleAgents.roi: Fewer missed grant deadlines and reduced staff time on compliance paperwork

multiAgent.name: Public Disclosure Swarm
multiAgent.description: A supervisor-led team that moves a public records request from intake to a redaction-reviewed response, with a human records supervisor making every release decision.

supervisor.name: Records Supervisor Agent
supervisor.responsibilities: Owns the request lifecycle, sequences intake → search → exemption review → response drafting, and escalates any exemption ambiguity or active-investigation record to a human records supervisor and legal counsel.
supervisor.routingLogic: New request → Intake Agent; document location → Retrieval Agent; possible exemption (RCW 42.56.230, victim/juvenile info, ongoing investigation) → human legal review; routine, unambiguous records → Response Drafting Agent.

subAgents.name: Intake Classifier Agent
responsibilities: Parse the request for date range, subject, and record type
Identify the responsible unit(s) holding responsive records
Flag requests naming an ongoing investigation or a minor for mandatory legal review
subAgents.contextHandoff: Scoped request definition to the Supervisor

subAgents.name: Records Retrieval Agent
responsibilities: Search RMS, CAD logs (non-surveillance metadata only), and email archives for responsive records
Compile a candidate document set with source and date
Never accesses biometric, facial recognition, or predictive-policing systems
subAgents.contextHandoff: Candidate document set to the exemption review step

subAgents.name: Exemption Flagging Agent
responsibilities: Highlight likely-exempt content (victim/witness PII, juvenile records, active investigation material) per RCW 42.56.230
Never finalizes a redaction or release decision
Prepares a side-by-side original/redacted-suggestion view for staff
subAgents.contextHandoff: Flagged document set with suggested redactions, unresolved

subAgents.name: Response Drafting Agent
responsibilities: Draft the response letter citing applicable exemptions
Log final disposition once a human approves release
subAgents.contextHandoff: Draft response package for records supervisor sign-off

multiAgent.conflictResolution: Any request touching an active investigation, a minor, or a victim/witness routes to a human records supervisor and legal counsel before any release. No agent in this swarm makes a final redaction or release decision. Exemption disagreements between agents default to the most restrictive (least disclosed) suggestion pending human review.

workflow.label: Input
workflow.description: Capture a public records request, report-drafting request, scheduling need, or grant deadline from staff or the public portal.

workflow.label: Reason
workflow.description: Supervisor agent classifies the task type and checks it against the allowed-use list before routing — anything resembling surveillance, biometric matching, or individual risk scoring is rejected, not routed.

workflow.label: Tool Execution
workflow.description: Agents search records, draft text, or assemble schedules/compliance packets using only administrative systems — no facial recognition, ALPR analytics, or predictive-policing tools are in the toolchain.

workflow.label: Human-in-the-Loop
workflow.description: A records supervisor, watch commander, or officer reviews and approves every report, redaction, schedule, or disclosure before it is final.

workflow.label: Output
workflow.description: Approved report, records response, schedule, or compliance filing is released; the underlying request/approval trail is logged for audit.

legacySystems: Paper case files and scanned archives
security: No facial recognition, biometric matching, or predictive-policing agents — excluded per RCW 43.386 and department policy
No new surveillance-technology use without Council-approved Surveillance Impact Report per Seattle Municipal Code 14.18 (Seattle-area agencies)
Every redaction, disclosure, and report requires human sign-off before release
Role-based access separating records/admin agents from CAD, evidence, and investigative systems
Full audit trail of every agent suggestion and human approval/override
